public_rationale: The ordinary payback reading holds. Continued unrecovered spending adds to what must eventually be earned back. At a positive required return, waiting also raises the future payoff needed to justify an existing investment. This supports the financial mechanism, not an unconditional prediction about AI profitability.
limitations: The conclusion assumes continued expenditure or a positive opportunity cost.
Cost reductions, reduced investment or lower required returns can change the burden.
The evidence does not establish the claimed breadth of agreement.

statement.excerpt: For Goldman to suddenly turn on the AI movement suggests that it’s extremely anxious about the future of generative AI, with almost everybody agreeing on one core point: that the longer this tech takes to make people money, the more money it's going to need to make.

our_interpretation: Read this as a claim about investment payback: delaying returns while investment continues increases the eventual earnings needed to justify that investment.
Hold the required return and other business assumptions constant. Continuing expenditure and a positive opportunity cost are implicit in the surrounding investment discussion.
This assesses the financial relationship, not whether almost everybody agreed or Goldman Sachs felt anxious.
No individual company's financial metric or amount is claimed, so metric_scope is null.
criteria.support_condition: Investment analysis and ordinary cash-flow arithmetic show that additional unrecovered spending or a longer wait at a positive required return increases the eventual payoff needed.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Under the same spending and required-return assumptions, delaying payback does not increase the eventual payoff required.

The textbook explains compounding at a positive rate. Applied to a fixed investment hurdle, this means a later payoff must be larger to have the same present value; that application is the evaluator's inference.
